name: Synthetic English Answer-Set Consistency Benchmark
description: Synthetic English benchmark subset created to exercise controlled set-theoretic relations among answer sets. The file contains 150 benchmark items with four related questions per item.

distribution.name: Synthetic English benchmark TSV
distribution.description: 150 synthetic benchmark items created to exercise controlled equivalence, subset, and complement relations.

recordSet.name: synthetic_en
recordSet.description: Rows from synthetic.tsv. Each row is a synthetic benchmark item with four related questions.

field.name: synthetic_en/Q3
field.description: Question targeting a constrained subset of Q1.

rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of large language models on controlled answer-set consistency tests.
Stress-testing prompting or post-processing strategies on known equivalence, subset, and complement patterns.
Not recommended as a standalone training corpus or as evidence of real-world deployment readiness.
rai:dataBiases: Synthetic construction reflects author choices about relation templates and topic selection.
The questions may be cleaner and more regular than naturally occurring user queries.
rai:dataLimitations: Because the subset is synthetic, performance may not transfer directly to naturally authored QA inputs.
The small size limits statistical power for narrow subgroup analyses.
The dataset is diagnostic and should not be used as a broad measure of factual QA ability.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The released file contains synthetic benchmark questions only and is not intended to include personal or sensitive user data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: This subset can help improve reliability analysis for QA systems by providing controlled test cases. A misuse risk is to over-generalize synthetic benchmark success to real-world safety, fairness, or truthfulness.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Synthetic benchmark generation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Synthetic items were authored or generated to create controlled question sets with intended set-theoretic relations.
